liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The China Cat intro is described as extremely crisp and precise [8]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): Reviewer considers this Eyes among the tightest ever played [8]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Sugar Magnolia is called incendiary, with Jerry's guitar and singing both strong across the show [16]
- **One More Saturday Night** (1 review): Saturday Night is called incendiary, with Bobby's vocals spirited [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Filer - Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **GoinÃÂ Down The Road FeelinÃÂ Bad**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd73-11-25.sbd.sacks.2213.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 201 min; rated 4.61/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: Vocals sound strongly clear for 1973, avoiding the thin, tinny quality that often affects recordings from that year; Reviewer calls the soundboard sound close to perfect throughout; Reviewer finds the recording sounds outstanding [7][8][15]
- **gd1973-11-25.150897.sbd.patched.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 22 songs; 176 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1973-11-25.150853.sbd.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 22 songs; 175 min [4]
- **gd1973-11-25.sbd.miller.113007.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 174 min; rated 4.75/5 by 16 [2]

## Around the show

- Promoter Barry Fey printed 'Feyline Field' on tickets; the show was really at Tempe's Diablo Stadium, a minor league ballpark [11]
- The small outdoor ballpark was dwarfed by the large sound system [11]
- A 15-year-old attendee was backstage; a boyfriend from Guadalajara photographed from the stage, and it was cold [14]
- Barry Fey had bought the old Tempe Diablo stadium and staged a series of shows there, including Allman Brothers, Leon Russell and Traffic [19]
- This Tempe show closed out the west coast leg of the Dead's fall tour [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-11-25.sbd.sacks.2213.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Filler tracks mid-show (Me & My Uncle, The Other One, Mexicali Blues, Wharf Rat) come from the 1971-12-04 Felt Forum show; Five filler tracks from another show sit in the middle of this recording; the reviewer removed them; Transfer work credited to Darrin Sacks and praised as excellent [1][9][12][15]
- **gd1973-11-25.150897.sbd.patched.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 13, 2020; source: SBD > Reel Master > Dat (44.1k) [3]. Also: Soundboard to cassette master to reel to reel (Panasonic RS1506) to Tascam DA-3000 at DSF 1-bit/5.6MHz; Patched version of an earlier release, with fixes in Playing in the Band and Let It Grow; patch source from Matt Smith; Pitch correction settings were provided by Joe B. Jones [3]
- **gd1973-11-25.150853.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 8, 2020; source: SBD > Reel Master > Dat (44.1k) [4]. Also: Upgrade over the uploader's earlier transfer of this show, using Joe B. Jones's pitch correction settings [4]
- **gd1973-11-25.sbd.miller.113007.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Feyline Field - November 25, 1973](https://www.dead.net/show/november-25-1973) [23]
